pairs.subject: agent-cli-transport
pairs.evidence: src/athena/harness/transports.py:276 a stopped run is ended by an unconditional proc.kill() of the direct child only: no polite rung, no deadline, no process-tree kill and no record of which rung ended it, so a shim's grandchildren outlive a wall or cancel (termination-and-reaping). Re-judged 2026-10-24: the 2026-10-14 findings on the probe (engines.py:92,207) and the key strip (transports.py:95,233) are now realized; they no longer count.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/harness/engines.py:207 the zero-token sign-in check runs through child_env, the spawn's environment, at a dated version floor (engines.py:92) and answers None when it cannot read the verdict (engines.py:222); residual: below the floor or on an unparsed version the fallback at engines.py:243 still reads a credential file's existence as logged_in

src/athena/harness/transports.py:233 the single spawn door builds the child environment through child_env, which strips every engine key (dated table at transports.py:95, 2026-10-16) after merging base and extra, with no per-call opt-out; pinned by tests/harness/test_cli_harness.py:545

src/athena/harness/transports.py:244 stderr is read on its own pipe and kept as a bounded tail, stdin is closed and its write guarded (transports.py:251); but src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:404 accumulates the answer with no total byte cap and no kill on breach (only a per-line 8 MiB limit, transports.py:40)

src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:58 the stance is one pre-set flag set (claude --restricted + dontAsk) and codex -s read-only (cli_harness.py:262): no enforcement class recorded, no allow/deny layers, no detection of a silent downgrade
src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:58 nothing reads the in-force stance, the billing direction or the injected context back from the child; the host's intent (argv and env) is trusted

src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:209 the invocation shapes (claude argv, codex argv at :262, CLAUDE_EXTRA_ARGS at :58) carry no verified-on date, tool version or method, no run-ceiling or idle-budget row; only the status checks (engines.py:92), the key table (transports.py:95) and the failure signatures (cli_harness.py:163) are dated

src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:360 a stored thread is released and the round asked again once only for the closed RESEED set {gone, poisoned} (cli_harness.py:67), rebuilt from the turn's own history; timeouts and other failures keep the binding
src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:55 the CLI's own tools are kept off and a page is operated only through the host's gate, so the child has no mid-turn approval request to route

src/athena/harness/engines.py:139 the probe never raises and answers a status with a reason, the spawn resolves the binary as the probe does (transports.py:225) and an OSError becomes a typed TransportError (transports.py:240); rung selection and labels live outside this context
src/athena/harness/transports.py:276 direct-child kill() only, no ladder, no tree, no rung recorded; the child is reaped (transports.py:277 await proc.wait())

pairs.registryProposal: output-normalization asks to preserve a bounded prefix of raw output in the error; this repo refuses on purpose (ADR 0109, a CLI's error text can quote the request) and keeps the tool's own classification as a closed class plus fixed sentence (cli_harness.py:62-78,139). The technique could name classify-then-discard as the conformant shape when the raw text may carry user content.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/athena/harness/rounds.py:240 a closed stream or cancel ends the turn as the cause 'cancelled' (and the wall as 'timeout', rounds.py:195) with cost_estimated=True (rounds.py:404) while the metered generation's outcome at the provider is unknown: there is no first-class indeterminate outcome for a killed model call, and the spend is flagged as a floor, never reconciled (indeterminate-closure-on-interruption). Re-anchored from the 2026-10-15 :187.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/harness/rounds.py:240 cancel writes reason 'cancelled' for a call whose outcome is unknown; 'outcome_unknown' exists in the vocabulary (src/athena/contracts/harness.py:143, ADR 0101) but only tool calls use it, not an interrupted generation

src/athena/harness/rounds.py:359 the ledger record of a call (result.tool_calls) is appended before gate.run_tool answers, so a refused call is still in the row; the three hooks are fixed constructor arguments (src/athena/harness/engines.py:248), not an indexed list
src/athena/harness/engines.py:248 the hook set is the caller's gate, ledger and truncation objects; the harness loads no contributed hooks or code, so there is no extension surface to tier

pairs.subject: session-continuation
pairs.evidence: src/athena/harness/rounds.py:212 on the last permitted round (MAX_ROUNDS = 8, rounds.py:56) the batch is still dispatched through the gate and executors although the loop ends at rounds.py:177 and no reasoning call will read the results (history.append at rounds.py:235 is never consumed), then the turn is summarised as success: side effects and approval cards for a batch nobody reads (boundary-applied-stop). Re-anchored from the 2026-10-17 :187.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/harness/rounds.py:212 a stop known before dispatch (round budget spent) does not refuse the batch with not-executed results; the wall stop is applied at the round boundary (rounds.py:184) and is conformant

src/athena/harness/rounds.py:85 the turn's wall and told-set are per-turn state reset at turn start (rounds.py:172) and held thread-locally since d7c00718, and every terminal path writes the row with its usage (rounds.py:240, :244, :258); the key is the thread, a proxy for the session that holds only while a turn locks its thread (ADR 0141), and _last (rounds.py:419) is still shared across threads
src/athena/harness/rounds.py:56 the harness has a fixed eight-round budget and no keep-working mode, record or lease to enforce at a yield
src/athena/harness/rounds.py:177 a bounded for-loop over MAX_ROUNDS with a once-per-name told-set (rounds.py:337); there is no unbounded loop to detect stuckness in

pairs.registryProposal: Technique-shaped resonance: the golden path's precondition is a keep-working continuation mode, which this bounded round loop lacks; only boundary-applied-stop (its use_when names the last-round batch exactly) and gate-state-lifetimes reach it. Eight of ten techniques are not-applicable here; the matcher is right on the two, and a note in the golden path that a fixed round budget is in scope for those two would stop the pair reading as weak.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/athena/harness/rounds.py:175 the turn's opening message (frame plus the user's words) and each later results message are composed after the blocks are hashed (rounds.py:168) and checked (rounds.py:169), so the text actually sent on stdin (cli_harness.py:447-451) has no recorded digest: the ledger holds block hashes only, not what was sent (fingerprinting-and-cache-keys, record what was sent at the send site). Re-anchored from the 2026-10-15 :399, which now falls on a docstring.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:343 a resumed CLI session is compared against the static half it was opened with and a changed half opens a new session (the session gate, stamp kept beside the session); the per-prompt ledger digest covers blocks only (rounds.py:168)

pairs.subject: voice-io
pairs.evidence: src/athena/channels/voice/tts.py:1 the speech door, the spoken budget and every pipeline voice-io governs live in channels/voice; this context only lets a model write one capped TTS: line (src/athena/harness/op_grammar.py:142) and passes it through. The match was lexical (engine/engines): an engine here is an LLM engine (src/athena/harness/engines.py:3), not a speech engine.

declined.subject: mcp-tools
declined.reason: Left unknown, not judged. The golden path excludes the model's own function-calling format; this context's tool contract is Athena's in-process OP: grammar behind a gate (src/athena/harness/op_grammar.py, rounds.py:360), with no MCP wire here. Only untrusted-result-handling resonates (the nonce fence at rounds.py:470), and prompt-safety is the better governing subject. Judging it would manufacture either a deviation or a not-applicable from a technique-shaped resonance.

proposedPairs.subject: subprocess-lifecycle
proposedPairs.reason: transports.py is the single spawn door: spawn-contract, termination-and-reaping (the kill without a ladder at transports.py:276), decode-child-output-per-line and host-resource-protection (PeakMemory, transports.py:356) are its techniques; agent-cli-transport borrows them rather than restating them.

proposedPairs.subject: model-call-outcome-integrity
proposedPairs.reason: the harness decides what a model call's result means: no_answer for a blank run (rounds.py:252), usage_limit (cli_harness.py:435), timeout vs cancelled, cost_estimated on a cut round (rounds.py:404).

proposedPairs.subject: cost-metering
proposedPairs.reason: TurnResult and LedgerHook write one row per turn with tokens, cost_usd, cost_estimated and peak_mb (contracts/harness.py:163, rounds.py:411).

proposedPairs.subject: prompt-safety
proposedPairs.reason: tool results are fenced with a fresh nonce before they re-enter the model (rounds.py:461-471) and prompt blocks carry an untrusted flag (contracts/harness.py:46).

proposedPairs.subject: hitl-approval
proposedPairs.reason: GateHook (hooks.py) files approval cards and refuses unattended writes; the map matched the context to no approval subject.
